problem: The paragraph is framed as "where this thesis parts company with the authors whose instrument it borrowed", and the headline divergence is that "the rank-based family as a family" failed to transfer. But the calibrated set this chapter attributes to Miller two pages earlier (line 211-213) contains exactly one rank-based metric --- Normalised Inverse Rank --- and NIR is the one metric that survived the port. The two rank-based failures are panel-tau and \texttt{spearman\_expr}, neither of which is in the set the chapter says Miller endorsed, so nothing about them is a divergence from Miller. The one genuine divergence on their endorsed set is weighted $R^2\Delta$, and it is demoted to a subordinate aside in the next sentence. The metric chapter gets the order right: it leads with "their calibrated set does not transfer intact" carried by \texttt{weighted\_r2}, and treats rank-based-ness separately as a claim about "the calibration literature's preference for rank-based metrics" (Investigation-v4.tex:570, 633-638). An examiner who checks which of Miller's metrics actually failed will find the promoted claim is not about Miller and the demoted one is.
quote: What does not transfer is the rank-based family as a family --- two of those four negatives are themselves rank-based [...] The fourth negative is the weighted $R^2$ variant implemented here, which their analysis rates as calibrated
fix: Invert the emphasis to match §res-metrics: lead with the actual divergence --- the one member of their calibrated set audited here besides NIR, our weighted $R^2\Delta$ implementation, comes out negative --- then make the rank-based point as the broader, non-Miller-specific observation it is in the chapter ("the field's preference for rank-based metrics does not survive the port: the two rank-based rivals audited here, neither of them in Miller's set, both invert").

problem: The stated reason is wrong and cannot support either half of the sentence. \texttt{revert\_center} predicts every gene at the constant middle rank $G/2$, so its shift from control is $G/2 - x$, not zero; it is control-copy, not revert_center, whose shift is identically zero. What actually happens is that the shift is an exact affine function of the control, so nothing survives the partialling — and, separately, that the prediction is constant, so every predicted rank ties and $\paneltau$ has no variance. The sentence as written explains neither: if the shift really were identically zero then $\hat y = x$ and $\paneltau(\hat y, y) = \tau(x, y)$ would be perfectly well defined, so the given reason contradicts the very fact it is offered for. The artifact agrees with the conclusion but not the reasoning — eval_endcell_linear.json carries no de_partial_k50 and no panel_tau entry for revert_center at any tier.
quote: The same predictor's partial-$\DEdr$ and $\paneltau$ are undefined rather than merely poor: its shift from control is identically zero, so there is nothing left to correlate once the control is regressed out.
fix: "The same predictor's partial-$\DEdr$ and $\paneltau$ are undefined rather than merely poor, and for two separate reasons: its shift from control is an exact linear function of the control, so nothing survives the partialling; and its prediction is constant, so every gene ties and there is no rank ordering to correlate."

problem: The claim box asserts a quantity its own section never derives. "Cell line, plate and dose projected out" is the context subspace of Step two, defined at lines 1074-1079 in the *next* subsection; the 0.883 figure lives in Table 3.x two subsections later. No forward pointer is given. Worse, the word "instead" has no antecedent in the section: the body paragraph immediately above closes on the opposite framing — "the between-drug to within-drug variance ratio collapses about three-fold across the final layers, so the drug is present throughout but geometrically de-emphasised as the output approaches" (lines 1036-1038) — and nothing bridges the two. This is the visible seam of the decodability-with-depth reconciliation: the claim box was rewritten to the reconciled position and the body paragraph beneath it was left in the old one.
quote: with cell line, plate and dose projected out the series rises with depth instead, to $88\%$ at the deepest.
fix: Bridge it in the body first, at the end of the paragraph ending line 1043: "That de-emphasis is of the raw geometry. Once the batch structure the drug is confounded with is projected out --- the construction of §res-used --- the series moves the other way, and that dissociation is what the next section is built on." Then the claim box's "instead" and its $88\%$ have an antecedent, and add "(§\ref{sec:res-used})" after "$88\%$ at the deepest".

problem: The three stratum gaps just quoted (+0.0351 near, +0.0716 orth, +0.1429 opposite) are each measured against their OWN stratum's scrambled partner -- fig-repair.json's gap array is indexed by strata [near, orth, opposite]. Only the third is read against the `opposite` comparator; the second is read against `orth`, which this chapter's own res-generalisation section calls "the neutral `orth` partner" (l.2088) and the direct 0.550/0.501/0.423 ordering (l.2095) singles out `opposite` alone as non-neutral. So the qualification is false for two of the three magnitudes, and the follow-on clause -- "the neutral-comparator magnitudes are adjudicated there" -- denies that any of the three is a neutral-comparator reading when +0.0716 is exactly that. It also contradicts l.1953-55 in the same section, which correctly treats `opposite` as one stratum of three: "only the `opposite` stratum excluding zero --- and `opposite` is the one stratum this chapter shows is not a null."
quote: Two qualifications ride with the magnitudes. They were read against the \texttt{opposite} comparator, which \S\ref{sec:res-generalisation} shows is not a null, so they are quoted here as a gradient and the neutral-comparator magnitudes are adjudicated there.
fix: Restrict the qualification to the stratum it applies to: "Two qualifications ride with the magnitudes. The \texttt{opposite} figure is read against a comparator \S\ref{sec:res-generalisation} shows is not a null, so the series is quoted here as a gradient; the \texttt{orth} rung is the neutral-comparator reading, and its magnitude is adjudicated there."

problem: The −0.017 entry is `diff_drug_same_plate` from vardecomp_matched.json -- the different-drug/same-plate control that this same section spends a paragraph voiding, on the ground that it "differs from the estimand in two ways at once, different drug and same cell line" and that "a negative control that differs in more than one way cannot" bound the estimand (l.1707-12). Filing it under "matched negative controls" with the reference "must be ≈ 0" credits it as a bound the text has just denied it can be. It also conflicts with the checks table three rows earlier, which names exactly one such control: "structure-matched negative control & the estimand itself; returns $-0.008$" (l.1723), and with this table's own caption, which is singular: "The matched negative control sits on zero" (l.1753).
quote: matched negative controls & $-0.017$, $-0.008$ & spanning zero & must be $\approx 0$ \\
fix: Split the row, or relabel: "structure-matched negative control & $-0.008$ & spanning zero & must be $\approx 0$" as the bounding control, with the same-plate control shown separately as "$-0.017$ at plate scope, $+0.485$ at cell-line scope --- voided, differs in two ways (text)".

problem: The grouping key omits the drug. The builder (endcell/ot/build_ot_targets.py, l.192-205) iterates conditions keyed `(cell_line, plate, drug, dose)` and couples the plate's control cells to *that condition's* treated cells; only the control side is pooled at (cell line, plate). As written, the coupling would run against all treated cells on the plate, pooling drugs -- which would make the barycentric target carry no drug information at all, and would make both ladder endpoints drug-free. That contradicts the consensus construction defined one sentence earlier at the per-(drug, cell line, dose) level (l.1352-53), the finding that the consensus arm shows "real between-condition variation" (l.1406), and the OT arm's own prompt sensitivity (+0.0292 against a neutral partner, l.1925-26). An examiner who traces the ladder will ask which treated cells enter $\pi$.
quote: \emph{Optimal transport} computes, for each (cell line, plate) group, a coupling $\pi$ between control and treated cells minimising $\sum_{ij}\pi_{ij}\lVert x_i - y_j\rVert^2$ under uniform marginals
fix: "...computes, for each condition (drug, cell line, plate, dose), a coupling $\pi$ between that plate's control cells and the condition's treated cells minimising..."

problem: The paragraph opens by claiming only one of the three arms passed all three diagnostics, then the third diagnostic is reported as passing for all three arms, with only the size of the margin differing. The concessive 'while ... for all three arms' directly contradicts the topic sentence. This reads as a survivor of the pre-withdrawal framing: forty lines later the section formally withdraws "OT achieved nothing" and concedes the optimal-transport control is not inert, so a sentence asserting that only the residual arm passed everything is now the wrong frame as well as internally inconsistent.
quote: "Three further diagnostics on that build agreed, and only the residual model passed all three." ... "And while $\cos(\textrm{prediction}, \textrm{own truth})$ exceeded $\cos(\textrm{prediction}, \textrm{other drugs})$ for all three arms, the residual model's margin ($+0.084$) was roughly twice the optimal-transport arm's ($+0.049$) and three times the single-cell arm's ($+0.026$)."
fix: Change the topic sentence to a ranking rather than a pass/fail: "Three further diagnostics on that build agreed, and the residual model led on all three — outright on two, and by roughly a factor of two on the third, which all three arms clear."

problem: The chapter-summary table is captioned as the complete arm ledger, and the paragraph after it reinforces that reading by declaring which results are exempt. But four residual-frame arms that the chapter's own earlier ladder prints are absent from it: moa_lookup (0.552), control_copy (0.506), random (0.501), and the scramble 'near' partner (0.550, quoted at :2043 as part of the 0.550/0.501/0.423 ordering). The omission is self-evident inside the caption itself, which names three swap partners while the table lists two rows. The two field-attribution comparator arms (partner NIR 0.434 and 0.520, :2644-2645) are likewise neither in the table nor among the five declared exemptions.
quote: "Every arm on the calibrated metric, by frame." ... :2765 "Five results in this chapter are not arms and cannot appear in the table." ... :2758 "The \texttt{orth} comparator is one of three swap partners fixed before any scoring by residual cosine to the target ($+0.22$, $0.00$, $-0.20$)".
fix: Either drop the completeness claim ("The arms that carry this chapter's claims, by frame") or add the missing residual-frame rows (near 0.550, moa_lookup 0.552, control_copy 0.506, random 0.501) so the ledger matches tab:lookup.

problem: The reconciliation that rehabilitated the optimal-transport arm reached Claim 6, Table~\ref{tab:epsilon} and Table~\ref{tab:trainconfig}, but never reached Claim 2 or the appendix it rests on. Claim 2's third leg is carried by the swap-distance sweep, whose two columns are the single-cell AND optimal-transport checkpoints (l.976, and Appendix l.97). §res-encoding then withdraws the OT null in the strongest terms available -- "``OT achieved nothing'' is therefore withdrawn, and not weakly" (l.1949) -- and traces the consequence backwards explicitly to §res-epsilon ("The consequence reaches backwards", l.1956) but not to §res-blind. Compounding it: §methods-data legislates that "a null quoted without its budget cannot be read" and that "every generation-based evaluation reports ... the budget it was generated under" (l.403-406). The sweep is a generation-based null, and neither l.974-983 nor Appendix~\ref{sec:app-sweep} states its token budget -- while the chapter's headline measurement lesson is that an under-budgeted arm gets reported as a null. Claim 2's hedge names the plate rule, not the budget rule. An examiner who reads the spine in order meets a verdict box asserting a null from an instrument the chapter later disowns for one of its two arms.
quote: no more moved by a maximally dissimilar swap than by a similar one --- a bound from a sweep outside the within-plate rule (Appendix~\ref{sec:app-sweep}) rather than a canonical measurement.
fix: Add the budget caveat and the OT withdrawal to this leg, e.g. "...rather than a canonical measurement, and one of whose two checkpoints (optimal transport) §\ref{sec:res-encoding} later shows was scored under a budget that suppressed a real effect." Add the same pointer to Appendix~\ref{sec:app-sweep}, which currently presents the OT column as a clean null with no forward reference, unlike Table~\ref{tab:trainconfig}'s caption which does carry one.
